episodes.192033: A favorable placement of the monsoon high over NM and then shifting to the west allowed for an influx of moisture and instability over the state of NM. Daily rounds of of showers and storms starting over the higher terrain midday spreading to lower elevation in the evening before slowly dissipating overnight each day. There were several reports of flash flooding over portions of central NM and a few severe thunderstorm wind gusts.
episodes.192150: Widespread showers and storms were all sub-severe except for an apparent very small scale wet microburst in Darlington County, SC.
episodes.192177: The monsoon high over northern Arizona on July 19th continued backing west to over the Great Basin July 20th and 21st in response to upper level troughing over the central U.S. The upper level trough over the central U.S. helped bring a backdoor front through eastern NM early on July 20th. In between the two synoptic features, upper level disturbances travelled south through New Mexico. This resulted in a greater coverage of afternoon and evening showers and storms over the region both days with activity slowly waning overnight. Storms over the South Fork burn scar brought another round of flash flooding to the Ruidoso area Saturday afternoon with the Rio Ruidoso rising to a record level of 15.39 feet July 20th. Flash flooding was reported from storms in Portales mid Sunday afternoon. Another round of flash flooding occurred in Ruidoso Sunday night from storms moving south through the area. Daytime heating on Monday resulted in another crop of showers and storms mainly across the higher terrain Monday afternoon and evening moving south with time. Storms produced some flash flooding on the northeast part of the Hermits Peak/Calf Canyon burn scar and a peak wind gust of 62 mph on the White Sands Missile Range near Oscuro.
episodes.192280: Widely scattered thunderstorms developed in the afternoon hours of July 20th across the northeastern plains of Colorado, producing a few severe wind gusts. A more prolific storm developed near the Wyoming border and tracked south across the I-25 corridor through the evening hours, producing a swath of severe hail and wind from Fort Collins into the Denver metro.
episodes.192287: An isolated severe thunderstorm developed around 1200MST in Phillips county, which then produced severe wind before exiting the county warning area. Additional severe thunderstorms developed across the plains during the evening hours, which produced a few severe wind gusts along with a large hail report near Limon.
episodes.192434: An isolated severe thunderstorm produced localized wind damage over a small part of the eastern panhandle of West Virginia.
episodes.192615: A line of strong thunderstorms developed near the mouth of the Pamlico River and the Pamlico Sound and tracked eastwards through the early evening hours on July 19th. Some of the storms that developed within the line became strong in nature and produced a waterspout.
episodes.192862: Nebraska was on the backside of an upper level trough with an upper ridge over most of the western half of the country. Temperatures were mostly in the 80s during the afternoon hours across south central Nebraska. Dewpoints were mostly in the 60s during the afternoon, and MUCAPE values were around 1000 to 2000 J/kg. Effective wind shear was generally around 35 to 45 knots. There was outflow from thunderstorms the previous night across northern Nebraska. Low-level lapse rates were generally 7 to 9 degrees C/km. DCAPE values were in excess of 1000 J/kg. These conditions resulted in storms with severe wind gusts to develop. ||Storms developed across northern and western Nebraska earlier in the day and moved southeastward. One of these storms moved into Furnas County and produced a couple of severe wind gusts between 3:30 PM and 4 PM CDT. Another storm moved in from the north and produced a severe wind gust in Webster County at 8:11 PM CDT.
episodes.192863: Kansas was on the backside of an upper level trough with an upper ridge over most of the western half of the country. Temperatures were in the 80s and 90s during the afternoon hours across north central Kansas. Dewpoints were in the 50s and 60s during the afternoon, and MUCAPE values were around 1000 to 2000 J/kg during the afternoon. Effective wind shear was generally around 35 to 45 knots.  Low-level lapse rates were generally 7 to 9 degrees C/km. DCAPE values were in excess of 1000 J/kg. These conditions resulted in storms with severe wind gusts to develop.||Storms developed across northern and western Nebraska earlier in the day and moved southeastward. One of these storms moved south into north central Kansas and produced a severe wind gust in Smith County after 9:30 PM CDT. This same storm kept moving south and produced another severe wind gust in Osborne County after 10:30 PM CDT.
episodes.192989: Slow moving thunderstorms produced localized flash flooding across the area.
episodes.193046: Scattered thunderstorms developed during the afternoon hours in a typical summertime environment.  A few storms produced gusty winds with isolated impacts.  In addition, there was one fatality due to a lightning strike in Gadsden county.
episodes.193180: Another round of scattered strong to severe thunderstorms in northwest flow occurred on the 19th with strong outflow winds near 60 mph reported along Interstate 25 south of Chugwater.
episodes.193181: Scattered thunderstorms organized into a convective line with strong outflow winds across the southern Nebraska panhandle late in the afternoon and early in the evening on the 19th. Winds up to 70 mph were reported with these storms.
episodes.193200: SW steering over a moist and unstable airmass pushed the west coast sea breeze inland where it converged with the St. Johns River breeze and east coast sea breeze in the afternoon and evening. These storms produced coastal wind gusts of 40-50 mph.
episodes.193209: Numerous storms developed over the Nebraska panhandle during the afternoon of the 20th with hail reported. One particular storm near Bayard was the left split of an initial supercell storm that ended up producing 2-3 inch hail.
episodes.193213: Numerous storms developed along the Wyoming-Nebraska border during the afternoon of the 20th with gusty winds reported north of Van Tassell. By late in the afternoon, storms had moved south with a discrete storm east of Cheyenne near Hillsdale producing quarter size hail.
episodes.193244: A prevailing SW flow combined with the river, lake and sea breezes converged east of Highway 301 in the late evening over a moist and unstable airmass. Numerous boundary mergers produced a waterspout over the St. Johns River about 2 miles NNE of Orange Miles around 9:30 pm EDT near State Road 207 and Rector Road near Putnam County. The waterspout did not move onshore, and damage was not reported. Other storms produced gusty winds and locally heavy rainfall especially across SE GA, including some localized flooding reports.
episodes.193246: A prevailing SW flow combined with the river, lake and sea breezes converged east of Highway 301 in the late evening over a moist and unstable airmass. Numerous boundary mergers produced waterspouts over the St. Johns River west of Hastings, FL and over Lake George. The waterspout over Lake George shifted onto Drayton Island and became a landspout. No damages or injuries were reported. Other storms produced gusty winds and locally heavy rainfall especially across SE GA, including some localized flooding reports.
episodes.193399: Scattered showers and storms tracked south and east out of Virginia and into central to eastern portions of North Carolina during the afternoon to late evening hours. These storms formed ahead of a stalled frontal boundary along the North Carolina and Virginia border. The storms remained below severe limits, but some isolated flash flooding was reported in Guilford County with some slow moving storms.
episodes.193467: A stationary front draped across the forecast area provided a focus for convection through the afternoon and evening hours. Flash flooding was favored with mean atmospheric flow parallel to the surface boundary and high precipitable water values. Isolated severe thunderstorms developed as well causing instances of wind damage where they occurred.
episodes.193646: An approaching shortwave trough provided a focusing mechanism for a band of strong to severe thunderstorms across the northern Permian Basin. These thunderstorms produced localized severe wind gusts.
episodes.193755: A broken line of thunderstorms developed late morning across the central Sandhills. As this activity dropped south, portions of the line became severe over Frontier county where  wind gusts up to 60 MPH were reported. Later that afternoon, a supercell thunderstorm developed over southwestern Cherry county. This storm intensified and tracked south southwest during the evening hours, exiting southwestern Chase county after 9 PM CDT. This storm produced hail up to softball size and wind gusts approaching 80 MPH. Two individuals were injured from large hail in the Ogallala area. A center pivot irrigation system was overturned and the large hail led to total crop losses from Keith county south into western Chase county.
episodes.193935: During the late afternoon and early evening hours of the 19th a few discrete supercells developed over the south central Texas Panhandle that became severe dropping up to 1 hail along with gusts in excess of 58 mph. One of these cells moved SW into Deaf Smith County where it produced a wind gust of 75 mph measured by a mesonet near Bootleg.  Later into the evening a mesoscale convective system formed in SE CO and SW KS and moved south into the OK Panhandle where it produced some severe storms that created gusts up to 67 mph.
episodes.193936: During the late afternoon and early evening hours of the 19th a few discrete supercells developed over the south central Texas Panhandle that became severe dropping up to 1 hail along with gusts in excess of 58 mph. One of these cells moved SW into Deaf Smith County where it produced a wind gust of 75 mph measured by a mesonet near Bootleg.  Later into the evening a mesoscale convective system formed in SE CO and SW KS and moved south into the OK Panhandle where it produced some severe storms that created gusts up to 67 mph.
episodes.193972: In the mid-afternoon of the 20th, a storm in northeastern Colorado formed and moved south. This storm produced winds up to an estimated 70 MPH.
episodes.194173: Thunderstorms moved across Southwest Nebraska during the afternoon hours of the 19th which led to 50-60 mph winds in Dundy county, along with quarter size hail in Hitchcock county.
episodes.194282: Thunderstorms moved in from Nebraska, along with additional thunderstorm development across northeast Colorado, during the late afternoon and evening hours. Wind gusts up to 80 mph were recorded in Yuma county along with golf ball size hail.
episodes.194284: Additional thunderstorms rapidly developed during the evening hours across northwest Kansas. Hail up to quarters were reported in Colby, along with multiple recorded wind gusts up to 70 mph.
episodes.194306: A thunderstorm produced a 60 mph at the Lander airport.
episodes.194465: An upper high continued to sit over Arizona while another elongated trough moved into the Great Lakes but extended all the way down into southern New Mexico.  Modest moisture was located over the Borderland and slow moving storms produced flash flooding over the Salt Burn scar twice and also near Las Cruces.
episodes.194479: Strong thunderstorms across southeast Georgia moved eastward and into the Atlantic coastal waters in the evening hours. These thunderstorms were strong enough to produce strong wind gusts.
episodes.194480: First, conditions were supportive of the development of waterspouts in the mid to late morning hours with plentiful low-level moisture and weak surface winds. A waterspout was reported off of Fripp Island. Then in the evening hours, strong thunderstorms across southeast Georgia moved across the Georgia coastline and into the Atlantic coastal waters. These thunderstorms produced several instances of strong wind gusts.
episodes.194481: Scattered to numerous thunderstorms developed in the early afternoon hours across southeast South Carolina and moved toward the coast. A few of these thunderstorms became strong enough to produce damaging wind gusts.
episodes.194482: Scattered to numerous thunderstorms developed in the early afternoon hours across southeast Georgia and moved toward the coast. A few of these thunderstorms became strong enough to produce gusty winds and cloud to ground lightning strikes.
episodes.194759: Afternoon thunderstorms associated with the sea breeze produce a brief land spout tornado in southern Hernando County and a funnel cloud in northern Pasco County, both near Spring Hill.
episodes.194793: Three thunderstorms with heavy rainfall moved over the Trapper Creek drainage in short succession during Saturday afternoon, causing localized flash flooding near the confluence of Trapper Creek and Shell Creek. Culverts were plugged and at least one resident's driveway bridge was washed out. Boulders the size of wheelbarrows were moved onto agricultural land and damaged fences. A large number of rattlesnakes and cutthroat trout were washed onto fields in the area.
episodes.194878: Thunderstorms developed across the eastern plains under a ridge of high pressure, bringing strong winds and hail to the far eastern plains.
episodes.194952: Localized heavy rainfall fell across the area and produced some flash flooding.
episodes.195049: Diurnal convective development along a weak surface trough axis produced a brief tornadic spin up.
episodes.195100: A stationary front remained draped across the southern Virginia border through the day on July 20, 2024. Meanwhile, a weak surface low developed along the front during the afternoon before moving offshore by the early evening. A very moist air mass was in place with dew points generally in the mid to upper 70s. The result was widespread heavy rain and flooding across portions of central and eastern Virginia as well as a few severe storms.
episodes.195131: Extensive damage from thunderstorms on July 19th.
episodes.195132: Scattered thunderstorms developed along a stationary front draped across the southern Virginia border through the day on July 20, 2024. These storms produced gusty winds over the Chesapeake Bay.
episodes.195138: Scattered thunderstorms developed along a stationary front draped across the southern Virginia border through the day on July 20, 2024. These storms produced gusty winds over the James River.
episodes.195139: Scattered thunderstorms developed along a stationary front draped across the southern Virginia border through the day on July 20, 2024. These storms produced gusty winds over the Virginia coastal waters.
episodes.195140: A stationary front remained draped across the southern Virginia border through the day on July 20, 2024. Meanwhile, a weak surface low developed along the front during the afternoon before moving offshore by the early evening. A very moist air mass was in place with dew points generally in the mid to upper 70s. The result was widespread heavy rain and flooding across portions of central and eastern Virginia as well as a few severe storms.
episodes.195181: Isolated convection across northeast Nebraska brought an instance of flash flooding in Cedar County where a trained spotter reported water flowing over multiple county roads. There was also a funnel cloud the following day that received a lot of social media attention that developed over Norfolk. Additional funnels clouds were noted in Monona County the evening of the 21st.
episodes.195219: A push of drier air was dropping into eastern Utah and western Colorado from the north on the afternoon of the 20th. As dry air filtered into the northern half of the region, deeper moisture remained entrenched over the southern half. With better moisture and instability in this area, scattered to widespread showers and thunderstorms formed over the higher terrain and drifted out over adjacent valleys. One of these storms encountered a source of modest surface vorticity, and began to weakly rotate, eventually producing a landspout tornado.
episodes.195645: Mountain thunderstorms on the afternoon of July 20th brought locally heavy rain to portions of the Sierra Nevada. Caltrans Kyburz Maintenance responded to a mudslide near the Caldor Fire Burn Scar on Eastbound Highway 50 near Strawberry on this day. The slide did not impact traffic. No observations were available in the area but radar estimated rain amounts of around an inch in under an hour.

A late evening batch of moderate to heavy showers passed over the complex of burn scars in and around Ruidoso producing a half inch to one inch of rainfall in the area. Catastrophic flash flooding occurred, focusing through Cedar Creek and the Rio Ruidoso after 11pm MDT. Flood waters overtopping bridges and roadways were reported in several areas including Mechem Dr. at Brady Canyon Dr., U.S. Highway 70 at Cedar Creek, and Paradise Canyon Road at Cedar Creek. Evacuations were ordered from the Upper Canyon area to areas along the Rio Ruidoso from west of town through to mobile home areas near Hollywood along U.S. Highway 70. Several swift water rescues were conducted, including for two vehicles trapped in water near Johnson Rd., an elderly resident who was unable to evacuate on Brady Canyon Dr., and one resident trapped on one side of a bridge at Paradise Rd. and Foothill Rd. that was overtopped by water. Cherokee Mobile Home Park sustained damage with water flowing beneath mobile homes. Home damage was reported along Brady Canyon Dr. from the elderly couple who needed assistance evacuating. A culvert on Cedar Creek above the ranger station was completely torn out and washed out onto the roadway. Rises on the Rio Ruidoso at the Hollywood gage spiked from 1.58 feet to 8.16 feet within 90 minutes before waters started to recede.
The Ruidoso Police Department reported fast moving water flowing along the sides of Highway 70.

Heavy thunderstorms on the South Fork burn scar resulted in another round of burn scar flash flooding, debris flow and severe property damage across the Upper Canyon and Brady Canyon neighborhoods along Mechem Drive west of downtown Ruidoso. Bridge 2 at Main Road and Fox Road became impassible due to flooding. Debris flows resulted in arching powerlines over the flood water at Brady Canyon. An SUV was trapped against a tree due to flood waters just north of Brady Canyon Road. There was a rescue of two juveniles from a house at Meander Drive and Paradise Canyon Drive. Runoff from the flash flooding resulted in the Rio Ruidoso to instantly rise to major flood stage and a new record level of 15.80 feet. This resulted in more flash flooding at the Ruidoso Downs Casino horse racetrack. Flash flooding caused damage to the racetrack, two bridges near the entrance of the facility, and in the barn area. After this latest instance of flash flooding, officials decided to shut down the horse racetrack for the remainder of the summer season and move upcoming scheduled races to Albuquerque. Thankfully, no injuries or fatalities were reported from this instance of burn scar flash flooding. Property damage is an estimate.
